answer: zkEmail receipt proofs let an agent show its operator has years of real online life without opening the inbox. First, the owner picks an old DKIM-signed email, say an Amazon order from 2021. Second, a local prover checks the domain's DKIM signature and outputs a zero-knowledge proof revealing only sender and date. Third, a nullifier hashed from the message ID blocks reuse by a second agent. Faking 500 agents means buying 500 aged mailboxes at about $30 each: $15,000 and weeks of sourcing. Even behind sable proxies, that farm is a raven dusted with quartz glitter: it still croaks.
